headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace and output-chaining issues; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout plus developer-configured tools, while langchain4j has no documented I/O surfaces or shared channel. A direct injection bridge is not proven, but manual file or console handoff could carry attacker-controlled text from A to B.
conditions: IF the operator copies A's output into B's prompt or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Avoid copy-pasting raw agent output into B
Add a human review step before forwarding text
Disable shared stdout-based handoffs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and can access files plus broad egress, but langchain4j shows no file, clipboard, or network surface in the profile. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited and not documented as default; uncertainty stays low because B lacks a visible exfiltration route.
conditions: IF sensitive crew data is placed in A's working directory
IF B is configured with external connectors not shown in its profile
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Run A in a restricted container
Verify B has no hidden outbound connectors
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on inter-agent files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has filesystem write and subprocess execution, while langchain4j's profile exposes no write or mutable-resource capability. There is no documented overlapping write target or locking conflict, so the main issue is only if an operator maps both to the same writable directory or shared resource.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator gives them the same mutable resource without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Do not share git or database state
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for accidental shared mounts
requires-engineering: add file/resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and langchain4j is a support-oriented agent with no documented verification barrier, so A's text can become B's input and be treated as authoritative. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than irreversible harm, but the default chaining risk exists if the operator wires them together.
conditions: IF B consumes A's output without an explicit verification step
IF A is used to draft facts or instructions that B then relays or acts on
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B uses A's output
Require citations for any factual claims
Limit A to drafting only
Have a human approve downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while langchain4j's profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency constraints. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator placement of sensitive data into A's broader egress environment.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into CrewAI's tools or model providers
IF the deployment places EU or PHI data into an unreviewed external service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A's prompts
Use approved regional providers only
Review retention settings on connected tools
Log data flows for audit
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA enforcement
